subject: c-info
title: C.INFO.------SOC.RT.DY.
description: Diagram in SR(TRS)II-22 (Social Reality / Trans-Information, Level Two) accompanying Braxton's claim: 'the achievements in world culture can provide some basis for viewing this cycle as a cycle — which is to say, a point in time and nothing more.' (C)C-INFO (the concept of composite information) is crossed with SOC-RT-DY (social-reality dynamics): the question is what composite-information produces when crossed with social-reality-dynamics — composite-information being the deeper field of world-cultural achievement against which the late-seventies cycle should be measured. (R)TM (reality of time) and (R)OBS (reality of observation) form the upper-right cluster. COS-P (cosmic principle) feeds into the subject from the lower-left. VT-DY (vibrational dynamics) sits between subject and partner. INFO-DY (information dynamics) sits below. PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) and PART (participation) anchor the lower-right output via a *dashed* edge — the conditional link between progressional-continuance and participation is load-bearing. Structural argument: composite-information crossed with social-reality-dynamics is mediated by vibrational-dynamics as central hub, with cosmic-principle as foundational upstream and reality-of-time plus reality-of-observation as upper outputs. The dashed PROG-CONT→PART edge is Braxton's structural diagnostic: even when composite-information is properly held and vibrational-dynamics functions as hub, the link from progressional-continuance to actual participation remains conditional. Real participation requires more than information and hub-function — it requires that the conditional edge be actually held by living people, which is exactly what 'a point in time' framing risks losing.
